title: Peristalsis is the muscle wave that moves a meal along the gut
summary: NIAMS says waves of muscle called peristalsis move food through the digestive system.
body: NIAMS says this muscle works without a person choosing the movement. Waves of those contractions, called peristalsis, move food through the digestive system. The page also says muscle at the far end pushes waste out. This card is the wave that carries a meal along. It is not a menu and not treatment for a sour gut.

sources.title: Health Lesson: Learning About Muscles
sources.author: National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases
sources.note: US government page, public domain. Last Updated June 2025. Smooth muscle section: peristalsis is waves of smooth-muscle contraction that help move food through the digestive system.
